short: Estimated cost and sampled error of the Häner baseline

statements.markdown: whose maximum error $\sim 10^{-6}$ is driven by the error in the square root computation
statements.note: Appendix F.2 reports a baseline error of about $10^{-6}$, attributing it mainly to the square-root computation; it does not give a uniform bound for the benchmark input words. Under its stated precision hypotheses, `arcsin_correctness` gives one table whose output satisfies the absolute-error bound for every valid represented input, and whose unitary the compiled program realizes as a clean subroutine on every disjoint register placement.

statements.markdown: We calculate a lower bound of the full circuit spacetime cost of $1.08\times 10^{8}$
statements.note: The fixed-width Newton workspace formula $n(m+4)$ gives 245 qubits at $n=35,m=3$. Appendix F.2 prices the polynomial and square-root blocks at $138{,}432$ and $302{,}144$ $T$ gates. Taking their sum times 245 gives the authors’ partial estimate of $107{,}941{,}120$.

statements.note: Fig. S10 routes either $x^2$ or $(1-x)/2$ to the polynomial using a comparison bit, with $x=|y|$. The circuit later uncomputes the comparison. The sketch starts with a zero output register. The estimate counts the selected evaluation blocks, and the modular-add interface in F.1 has an arbitrary initial output $b$.
